requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL only be used in the module definitions part.
requirements.original: a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
requirements.original: a) An import statement shall only be used in the module definitions part and not be used within a function definition and alike.

ambiguity.issue: "a function definition and alike" does not list the excluded constructs; the example also shows the control part. Chose all behaviour definitions and the control part.
readings: An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function, altstep or testcase definition or the control part.
An import statement SHALL NOT be used within a function definition or any other definition outside the module definitions part (e.g. component types, groups' members are allowed).

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL import only top-level definitions of a module that are visible to the importing module.
requirements.original: b) Only top-level visible definitions of a module may be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT import a top-level definition that is invisible to the importing module.
requirements.original: Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT import a definition that occurs at a lower scope than the module (e.g. a local constant defined in a function).
requirements.original: Definitions which are top-level but invisible to the importing module or which occur at a lower scope (e.g. local constants defined in a function) shall not be imported.

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: An imported definition IS imported together with its name and all its local definitions.
requirements.original: c) A definition is imported together with its name and all local definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local definition (e.g. a field name of a record type or an enumerated value) has meaning only in the context of the definition in which it is defined; e.g. a field name of a record type IS usable only to access a field of that record type.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: A local definition, e.g. a field name of a user-defined record type or an enumerated value, has only meaning in the context of the definitions in which it is defined, e.g. a field name of a record type can only be used to access a field of the record type and not outside this context.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: Importing an enumerated type IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
requirements.original: In particular, importing an enumerated type does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: EXAMPLE 5 states that in module B (which imports enumerated type MyEnumType) the constant "const MyEnumType enumY" is not allowed because enumerated values restrict global names, which seems to contradict this sentence. Chose the literal text; the example may mean that the clash is only forbidden in the context of the enumerated type.
readings: Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type without restriction.

Global names in the importing module MAY be equal to enumerated values of an imported enumerated type, except where the definition is in the context of that enumerated type (then clause 6.2.4 applies).

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: An imported definition IS imported together with all information of its referenced definitions that is necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions.
requirements.original: d) A definition is imported together with all information of referenced definitions that are necessary for the usage of the imported definition, independent of the visibility of the referenced definitions (see clause 8.2.5).

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.condition: module C imports from module B a definition that references a type defined in module A
requirements.canonical: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type defined in module A, the information necessary for the usage of that type IS automatically imported into module C.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: If module C imports a definition from module B that uses a type reference defined in module A, the corresponding information necessary for the usage of that type is automatically imported into module C (see example 6 below in this clause).

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.condition: module C imports value, template or local definitions of an enumerated type from module B
requirements.canonical: If module C imports from module B global value or template definitions (constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (formal parameters, component constants and variables) of an enumerated type, the enumerated values of that type ARE implicitly imported into module C and are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C.
requirements.original: In particular, if module C imports global value or template definitions (e.g. constants, module parameters, templates) or local definitions (e.g. formal parameters of templates, functions, etc. or constants and variables of component types) of an enumerated type from module B, the enumerated values of this type (i.e. the identifiers) are implicitly and automatically imported to module C. That is, the enumerated values are known when an enumerated value or template is used in module C (e.g. when an actual parameter is passed or a value is assigned to a component variable).

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: The implicit import of enumerated values IS NOT imposing the restriction of clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in the importing module.
requirements.original: Note that this implicit importing does not impose the restriction given in clause 6.2.4 on global names defined in module C.

requirements.subject: ent:referenced-definition
requirements.condition: the referenced definition is to be used in the importing module
requirements.canonical: A referenced definition that is to be used in the importing module SHALL be explicitly imported, either directly from its source module or by importing the import statements of a module that imports it.
requirements.original: e) If the referenced definitions are wished to be used in the importing module, they shall be explicitly imported either directly from its source module or indirectly by importing the import statements of a module importing it (see clause 8.2.3.7).

requirements.subject: ent:behaviour-description
requirements.canonical: When a function, altstep or testcase is imported, its behaviour specification and all definitions used inside it ARE NOT visible to the importing module.
requirements.original: f) When importing a function, altstep or test case the corresponding behaviour specifications and all definitions used inside the behaviour specifications remain invisible for the importing module.

ambiguity.issue: "test case" is used for the TTCN-3 testcase definition; "behaviour specification" is used where the semantic description says "behaviour description".

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.canonical: The language specification of an import statement SHALL NOT override the language specification of the importing module.
requirements.original: g) The language specification (see clause 8.1) of the import statement shall not override the language specification of the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.condition: a language specification is defined in the source module
requirements.canonical: If the source module defines a language specification, the language specification of an import statement importing from it SHALL be identical to the language specification of the source module.
requirements.original: h) The language specification of the import statement shall be identical to the language specification of the source module from which definitions are imported (see clause 8.2.3.8) provided a language specification is defined in the source module.

requirements.subject: ent:language-specification
requirements.condition: no language specification is defined in the source module
requirements.canonical: If the source module does not define a language specification, the language specification of the import statement IS taken as the language specification of the source module.
requirements.original: If not, the language specification in the import statement is taken as the language specification of the source module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.condition: the source module has no language specification and uses language concepts not part of the language specification given in the import statement
requirements.canonical: If the source module uses language concepts that are not part of the language specification taken from the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: If the source module uses however language concepts not being part of that language specification, this causes an error for the import statement.

ambiguity.issue: "that language specification" most likely refers to the language specification taken from the import statement when the source module has none (previous sentence); it could also refer to any language specification of the import statement.
readings: If the source module has no language specification and uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error.

If the source module uses language concepts not part of the language specification of the import statement, the import statement SHALL cause an error, whether or not the source module defines a language specification.

requirements.subject: ent:module-identifier
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name IS NOT imported.
requirements.original: i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.

requirements.subject: ent:module-identifier
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name SHALL NOT be used for referencing the imported module.
requirements.original: i) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the original module name is not imported and cannot be used for referencing the imported module.

requirements.subject: ent:local-module-name
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: A module renamed in the import clause SHALL be referenced using its new local name only.
requirements.original: The imported module can be referenced using the new local name only.

requirements.subject: ent:local-module-name
requirements.condition: the imported module is renamed in the import clause
requirements.canonical: If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module SHALL be unique in the scope of the importing module.
requirements.original: j) If an imported module is renamed in the import clause, the new local name of the module shall be unique in the scope of the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:importable-definition
requirements.canonical: Definitions with the same name defined in different modules ARE different definitions, even if their actual definitions are identical.
requirements.original: NOTE 7: Definitions with the same name defined in different modules are always assumed to be different, even if the actual definitions in the different modules are identical.

requirements.subject: ent:type
requirements.canonical: Importing a type that has the same name as a locally defined type results in two different types being available in the importing module.
requirements.original: For example, importing a type that is already defined locally, even with the same name, would lead to two different types being available in the module.

non_requirement.reason: identifiers of referenced definitions are not imported automatically: covered by TTCN3-CORE-8.2.3.1-062a
